questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

The mother as well as her children were brought to the police station for interrogation.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is -** 'Her children were brought'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the wrong usage of **subject-verb agreement.**
 
• If the **subject **is joined with **as well as** the verb will agree with the **first subject.** 
 
• Here, the first subject is **The mother** (singular) then we will use the **singular verb** which is **was.**
 
 
• **Example:** *Ram as well as his mother is coming.*
 
 
 
• In the above example as well as is connected with** Ram** which is **singular** so here we will use** Is.**
 
• If the **subject** is joined by **as well as, along with, together with, in addition to, beside, but, except, rather than, accompanied by, like, unlike, no less than, nothing but,** the verb will agree with the **first subject.**
 
• Use of **was/were**
 
 
• **Was:** He/she/it/name/singular.
 
• **were:** you/we/they/all/plural.

 
 
 

The correct sentence will be:* The mother as well as her children was brought to the police station for interrogation.*

​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f1d776c4ca45212685ca0930c2539d73a1d70923a3eebad6480bea0298a95b3.png] 

 
• दिए गए वाक्य में, त्रुटि विषय-क्रिया subject-verb agreement. समझौते के गलत उपयोग में है। 
 
• यदि विषय के साथ-साथ क्रिया को भी जोड़ा जाता है तो क्रिया पहले विषय first subject. से सहमत होगी।
 
• यहाँ, पहला विषय है माँ (एकवचन) Singular फिर हम एकवचन क्रिया का प्रयोग करेंगे जो कि wasथा।
 
 
• Example: *Ram as well as his mother is coming. *(उदाहरण: राम और उसकी माँ भी आ रहे हैं।)
 
 
 
• उपरोक्त उदाहरण में और साथ ही राम के साथ जुड़ा हुआ है जो एकवचन (singular) है इसलिए यहाँ हम Is का उपयोग करेंगे।

 

**सही वाक्य होगा: ***The mother as well as her children was **brought** to the police station for interrogation.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

I tried to contact her two or three times but _______ time there was no reply.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1) i.e. Each.**

 
• '**Each**' is used while referring to every particular thing separately.
 
• 'Both' is used when two things are referred together.
 
• 'All' means every.
 
• 'Any' means one of the following options.

So, option 1 is correct as the sentence refers to each time the speaker contacted the girl/woman.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.

We can reject options 1 and 2 as they are in the present tense. 'Awoke' is mostly used as an adjective whereas '**woke'** is used as a verb.

Here, we require a verb.

So, option 3 is the most appropriate answer.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. Adolescence.**

• Adulthood means the state or condition of being fully grown or mature.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

The master did not know who of the servants had broken the glass.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 
• Here 'servants' is a plural noun. 'Who' is used when we are referring to any person in general. **'Which**' can be used when we have a number of options to choose from. 
 
• The correct phrase would be- **which one of the servants**.
 
• So, only option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement

He does not tell lies, __doesn’t he__ ?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

 
• The group of underlined words is called **question tags** which are dependent on the main clause with a pronoun referring back to the noun in the main clause. If the main clause is positive, the question tag is negative and vice-versa.
 
• In the given sentence, **the main clause is negative so the question tag will be positive**. Among all the options there is only one positive question tag i.e.** does he.**
 
• So, only option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement

Have you __ever being by __New York?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

 
• The verb form of 'being' is incorrect. As the speaker is asking a question by using 'ever' we should use the **past participle form of the verb**. 'Being' is the continuous form of the verb which highlights an ongoing action.
 
• Instead of 'being', **we should use 'been'**.
 
• Also, the use of the preposition 'by' is incorrect. 'By' means with the help of something and here the sentence refers to visiting a place. We should use the **preposition 'to'**.
 
• So, only option 3 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Chris and I play tennis together regularly, but ________ of us can play very well.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. neither.**

 
• The sentence uses 'but' which means that the speaker introduces a contradictory statement after 'but'.
 
• We can reject options 1 and 2 as they would give the sentence positive meanings. 
 
• None is used when there are multiple options and not even one is true, hence option 3 is also rejected.
 
• **Neither is used when there are two options and not even one is true. **It means 'not the one nor the other of two people or things; not either.'
 
• Here, we have two people. Hence, we will use **'neither'**.
 
• So, only option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

You are not expect to do the work alone.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1) i.e. not expect.**

 
• The given sentence has an error in the verb form of 'expect'. The auxiliary verb 'are' is not in agreement with the verb form 'expect'. We **need to use a verb form which is in agreement with the particular verb**. So, we will use the **past participle form of the verb i.e. expected**.
 
• The correct phrase would be** 'not expected'.**
 
• So, only option 1 is correct.
